steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

# Quizzy Implementation Notes

## Stack
- Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, SQLite (storage/*.sqlite3), Puma, Propshaft (assets) + plain public/quizzy.css
- No Turbo/Hotwire: all forms are plain HTML (`local: true`) to keep QA browser tests deterministic.
- No external services: stylesheet + font copied verbatim to `public/` and served locally.

## Auth
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic on every `/moderate/*` route via `authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic`.
- Compares against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`; missing/wrong => 401.
- `/up` (rails/health) is outside `/moderate`, no auth.

## Data model
- `Quiz(title)` has_many `Question(position)` ordered by position.
- `Question(body, active:true, position)` has_many `Option(position)` ordered by position.
- `Option(text, correct:false, position)`.
- Positions assigned sequentially; move_up/down swaps neighbours then normalizes to 1..n.
- Preview answers stored only in encrypted cookie session (`session[:preview][quiz_id]`), never in DB.

## Key flows
- Quiz form: Title required (HTML + model), Save quiz redirects to quiz page. Edit reuses same partial; Delete quiz uses `onsubmit="return confirm(...)"` (native confirm).
- Question form: Question textarea required; option rows `options[i][text]` + `options[i][correct]`; 4 empty rows on new, existing rows on edit, `Add option` JS appends next-numbered row with labels `Option N` / `Option N is correct`. Active checkbox defaults true on new. Server filters blanks, validates >=2 options else "Add at least two options", >=1 correct else "Mark at least one option as correct". On failure re-renders with submitted rows, no DB write (transaction).
- Quiz page: `<ol class="question-list"><li class="card question-item">` each with Move up/down (POST), Active checkbox auto-submit (`onchange="this.form.submit()"`), Edit link, Delete button (native confirm). Correct options get `is-correct` (✓ green). Inactive dimmed with —.
- Preview: `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview?step=N` shows Nth active question. `POST .../preview/answer` records option_id in session. After answering shows Correct!/Wrong! + `is-revealed` (all correct highlighted). Next question / See score links; result shows `Score: X/Y`. `POST .../preview/reset` (Start over) clears session. Empty preview handled gracefully.

## Production concerns
- `config.hosts.clear`, `force_ssl=false`, `assume_ssl=false` for plain HTTP any-host.
- `config/database.yml` production => `storage/production.sqlite3`.
- `bin/serve` (executable): exports RAILS_ENV=production, `db:prepare`, `assets:precompile`, `exec rails server -b 0.0.0.0 -p $PORT`.
- `public/quizzy.css` + `public/Inter-latin.woff2` copied from mockups; layout uses `<link href="/quizzy.css">` to avoid digest issues.
- Allowed labels kept exactly as visible text + `<label for>` / `aria-label` for Capybara `fill_in`/`check`/`click_on`.
- Each quiz/question in own `<li>` with controls inside; switches are real checkboxes; deletes use native `confirm()`.

## Testing
- `test/integration/quizzy_test.rb` + `edge_test.rb` cover auth, CRUD, validations, ordering, toggle, preview, empty, multi-correct, confirm presence, li structure.
- Manual browser test with Cuprite/Chromium verified Add option JS, autosave, confirms, full preview flow.

## Export/Import (2026-10-07)
- Routes: `GET /moderate/import` (`imports#new`, helper `moderate_import_path`), `POST /moderate/import` (`imports#create`), `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` (`quizzes#export`, helper `export_moderate_quiz_path`). All under `Moderate::BaseController` (HTTP Basic).
- Quiz page (`quizzes/show`): added `Export` link next to `Preview` (`link_to "Export", export_moderate_quiz_path`). Index (`quizzes/index`): added `Import quiz` link next to `New quiz` (`link_to "Import quiz", moderate_import_path`).
- Export: builds `{"title", "questions": [{"text" (from body), "active" (bool), "options": [{"text", "correct" (bool)}]}]}` ordered by `position,id`, `JSON.pretty_generate`. View `quizzes/export.html.erb` has single `<pre id="quiz-export">` with `<%= @export_json %>` (escaped, `textContent` parses as JSON). No other `<pre>` on page. Only these keys, always writes `active`/`correct`.
- Import form (`imports/new.html.erb`): `form_with url: moderate_import_path, local: true`, `<label for="quiz_json">Quiz JSON</label>` + `<textarea id="quiz_json" name="quiz_json" aria-label="Quiz JSON" placehold",

    end
    player = current_player

      if wants_json?
        render json: player_state_json(nil), status: :unauthorized
      else
        redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code)
      end
      return
    end
    # Only when open
    if @game.open? && @game.current_question_id
      option_id = answer_option_param
      if option_id.present?

            ans = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, question_id: @game.current_question_id)

            ans.option = opt
            ans.save!
          rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
            # retry once on race: try to update existing
            begin

            rescue StandardError
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end

      render json: player_state_json(player.reload)
    else

    end
  end

  setup do

    ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"] = "secret"

  end

    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Live Talk")
    q1 = quiz.questions.create!(body: "Capital?", active: true, position: 1)
    q1.options.create!(text: "Paris", correct: true, position: 1)
    q1.options.create!(text: "London", correct: false, position: 2)
    q2 = quiz.questions.create!(body: "2+2?", active: true, position: 2)
    q2.options.create!(text: "4", correct: true, position: 1)
    q2.options.create!(text: "5", correct: false, position: 2)

    # Use Capybara sessions for isolation

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"

    assert_button "Start a game"

    assert_match %r{/moderate/}, current_url
    assert_text quiz.title
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    assert_button "Start"

    puts "JOIN URL: #{join_url_text}"
    assert_selector "#qr-code svg"
    code = join_url_text[/\/play\/([A-Z0-9]+)/i, 1]
    assert code, "no code"
    puts "CODE=#{code}"

    # Save moderator cookies? No, use separate sessions via using_session
    # For players, we need separate browser contexts (separate cookies).
    # Capybara using_session will share same browser? Actually using_session with same driver shares browser but different cookies? In Cuprite, each session is separate? Let's use separate sessions.

    using_session(:alice) do
      visit "/play/#{code}"
      assert_text "Your name"
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_on "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end

    # Back to moderator (default session) should see Players: 1 live
    # Note: default session is :default? After using_session, need to switch back?
    using_session(:default) do
      page.driver.headers = { "Authorization" => @auth }
      assert_text "Players: 1", wait: 10
    end

    using_session(:bob) do

      assert_text "Players: 2", wait: 10

  end

  end

    cur = list.find { |q| q.id == current_question_id }

    idx = list.index(cur)

  end

      .where("position > ? OR (position = ? AND id > ?)", question.position, question.position, question.id)
      .order(:position, :id).first
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  def answers_count_for(question_id = current_question_id)
    return 0 if question_id.nil?
    answers.where(question_id: question_id).count
  end

  def counts_per_option(question = nil)

      reload
      return false unless waiting?
      first = first_active_question
      if first.nil?
        update!(status: "ended", current_question: nil)
      else
        update!(status: "open", current_question: first, question_opened_at: Time.current)
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def finish!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false unless open?
      update!(status: "closed")
      true
    end
  end

      if cur.nil?

      if nxt.nil?
        update!(status: "ended")
      else
        update!(status: "open", current_question: nxt, question_opened_at: Time.current)
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def end!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false if ended?
      update!(status: "ended")
      true
    end
  end

  # --- Scoring & leaderboard ---

  def winners_n
    n = quiz.winners_count rescue 3
    n = n.to_i
    n = 3 if n.nil? || n < 1
    n
  end

  def points_text_for(points)
    "#{points} #{points == 1 ? 'point' : 'points'}"
  end

  def place_text_for(place, total)
    "Place #{place} of #{total}"
  end

  # Returns array of {player:, points:, total_ms:, place:, points_text:, place_text:, is_winner:}
  # Ordered by points DESC, total_ms ASC, player.id ASC. Place is sequential 1..n.
  def leaderboard
    pls = players.order(:id).to_a
    total = pls.size
    # Preload answers with options to avoid N+1
    # Group answers by player_id
    all_answers = answers.includes(:option).where(player_id: pls.map(&:id)).to_a
    by_player = all_answers.group_by(&:player_id)
    results = pls.map do |p|
      ans_list = by_player[p.id] || []
      points = 0
      total_ms = 0
      ans_list.each do |a|
        opt = a.option
        if opt && opt.correct?
          points += 1
          total_ms += (a.elapsed_ms || 0).to_i
        end
      end
      {
        player: p,
        points: points,
        total_ms: total_ms,
        is_winner: !!p.winner
      }
    end
    results.sort_by! { |r| [-r[:points], r[:total_ms], r[:player].id] }
    results.each_with_index do |r, idx|
      place = idx + 1
      r[:place] = place
      r[:points_text] = points_text_for(r[:points])
      r[:place_text] = place_text_for(place, total)
      r[:winner_text] = r[:is_winner] ? "Winner" : nil
    end
    results
  end

  def entry_for_player(player)
    return nil if player.nil?
    board = leaderboard
    board.find { |e| e[:player].id == player.id }
  end

  def top_label
    "Top #{winners_n}"
  end

  # Top N: first N of leaderboard with points>0 become winners
  def select_top_winners!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false unless ended?
      n = winners_n
      board = leaderboard
      winner_ids = board.first(n).select { |e| e[:points] > 0 }.map { |e| e[:player].id }
      # If fewer than N have points, all with points win (already covered since board.first(n) filtered)
      # But to be explicit: if number with points < n, winners = all with points
      # Our logic already does that because first(n) includes all with points when they are < n (since sorted)
      # However if board.size > n but points beyond n? No, all with points are at top, so first(n) covers.
      # Edge: if board.size < n, first(n) returns all, filtered gives all with points. Good.
      transaction do
        players.update_all(winner: false)
        players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
      end
      true
    end
  end

  # Draw: everyone with more points than N-th place wins automatically;
  # remaining prizes drawn at random among those with exactly N-th place points.
  # 0-point players never win. If fewer than N have points, all win.
  def draw_winners!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false unless ended?
      n = winners_n
      board = leaderboard
      # Filter helpers
      with_points = board.select { |e| e[:points] > 0 }
      winner_ids = []
      if with_points.size < n
        # Fewer than N have points: all win
        winner_ids = with_points.map { |e| e[:player].id }
      else
        # with_points.size >= n, so N-th place exists and has points>0
        # N-th place in full board (which equals N-th in with_points since 0s are last)
        nth = board[n - 1]
        nth_points = nth ? nth[:points] : 0
        if nth_points.nil? || nth_points <= 0
          # Defensive: if N-th has 0 (should not happen when with_points>=n), all with points win
          winner_ids = with_points.map { |e| e[:player].id }
        else
          auto = board.select { |e| e[:points] > nth_points }
          tie_group = board.select { |e| e[:points] == nth_points }
          remaining = n - auto.size
          # remaining should be >=1 and <= tie_group.size
          remaining = 0 if remaining < 0
          remaining = tie_group.size if remaining > tie_group.size
          drawn = tie_group.sample(remaining)
          winner_ids = (auto + Array(drawn)).map { |e| e[:player].id }
        end
      end
      transaction do
        players.update_all(winner: false)
        players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def reset_winners!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false unless ended?
      players.update_all(winner: false)
      true
    end
  end

  private

  def ensure_code
    return if code.present?
    20.times do
      candidate = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(5).upcase.gsub(/[^A-Z0-9]/, "X")
      # Ensure 5 chars, avoid ambiguous? keep simple
      candidate = candidate.ljust(5, "X")[0, 5]
      unless Game.exists?(code: candidate)
        self.code = candidate
        break
      end
    end
    self.code ||= SecureRandom.hex(3).upcase
  end
end

      # If current missing (deleted/inactive), safest is to end (avoid repeats).
      # UI already shows End quiz in this case (last_question? true), so advance should rarely happen.
      if cur.nil?
        update!(status: "ended")
        return true
      end
      nxt = next_active_after(cur)
      if nxt.nil?
        update!(status: "ended")
      else
        update!(status: "open", current_question: nxt, question_opened_at: Time.current)
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def end!
    with_lock do
      reload
      return false if ended?
      update!(status: "ended")
      true
    end
  end

  # --- Scoring & leaderboard ---

  def winners_n
    n = quiz.winners_count rescue 3
    n = n.to_i
    n = 3 if n.nil? || n < 1
    n
  end

  def points_text_for(points)
    "#{points} #{points == 1 ? 'point' : 'points'}"
  end

  def place_text_for(place, total)
    "Place #{place} of #{total}"
  end

  # Returns array of {player:, points:, total_ms:, place:, points_text:, place_text:, is_winner:}
  # Ordered by points DESC, total_ms ASC, player.id ASC. Place is sequential 1..n.
  def leaderboard
    pls = players.order(:id).to_a
    total = pls.size
    # Preload answers with options to avoid N+1
    # Group answers by player_id
    all_answers = answers.includes(:option).where(player_id: pls.map(&:id)).to_a
    by_player = all_answers.group_by(&:player_id)
    results = pls.map do |p|
      ans_list = by_player[p.id] || []
      points = 0
      total_ms = 0
      ans_list.each do |a|
        opt = a.option
        if opt && opt.correct?
          points += 1
          total_ms += (a.elapsed_ms || 0).to_i
        end
      end
      {
        player: p,
        points: points,
        total_ms: total_ms,
        is_winner: !!p.winner
      }
    end
    results.sort_by! { |r| [-r[:points], r[:total_ms], r[:player].id] }
    results.each_with_index do |r, idx|
      place = idx + 1
      r[:place] = place
      r[:points_text] = points_text_for(r[:points])
      r[:place_text] = place_text_for(place, total)
      r[:winner_text] = r[:is_winner] ? "Winner" : nil
    end
    results
  end

  def entry_for_player(player)
    return nil if player.nil?
"
}

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "module Moderate
  class GamesController < BaseController
    before_action :set_quiz
    before_action :set_game, only: [:show, :state, :start, :finish, :next_step, :end_quiz]

    def create
      @game = @quiz.games.create!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_game_path(@quiz, @game)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), alert: e.message
    end

    def show
      prepare_show
    end

    def state
      render json: moderator_state_json
    end

    def start
      @game.start!
      respond_after_action
    end

    def finish
      @game.finish!
      respond_after_action
    end

    def next_step
      # From closed: advance to next open or ended
      @game.advance!
      respond_after_action
    end

    def end_quiz
      @game.end!
      respond_after_action
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_game
      @game = @quiz.games.find(params[:id])
    end

    def prepare_show
      @active_count = @quiz.questions.where(active: true).count
      @players_count = @game.players.count
      @join_url = join_url_for(@game)
      # QR SVG
      begin
        require "rqrcode"
        qr = RQRCode::QRCode.new(@join_url)
        @qr_svg = qr.as_svg(
          offset: 0,
          color: "000",
          shape_rendering: "crispEdges",
          module_size: 6,
          standalone: true,
          use_path: true
        )
      rescue StandardError => e
        Rails.logger.warn("QR failed: #{e.message}")
        @qr_svg = %(<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><text x="10" y="50">QR</text></svg>)
      end

      if @game.open? || @game.closed?
        @current_question = @game.current_question
        # If current missing (deleted), try to handle gracefully: reload list
        if @current_question.nil?
          # No current: treat as waiting? But status is open/closed, need to show something
          @options = []
          @counts = {}
          @answers_count = 0
        else
          @options = @current_question.options.order(:position, :id).to_a
          @counts = @game.counts_per_option(@current_question)
          @answers_count = @game.answers_count_for(@current_question.id)
        end
        @progress = @game.progress_text
        @is_last = @game.last_question?
      else
        @current_question = nil
        @options = []
        @counts = {}
        @answers_count = 0
        @progress = nil
        @is_last = false
      end
    end

    def join_url_for(game)
      # Full URL with scheme for display and QR (same string)
      "#{request.base_url}/play/#{game.code}"
    end

    def moderator_state_json
      game = @game.reload
      quiz = @quiz
      players_count = game.players.count
      total = quiz.questions.where(active: true).count
      data = {
        status: game.status,
        code: game.code,
        quiz_title: quiz.title,
        join_url: "#{request.base_url}/play/#{game.code}",
        players_count: players_count,
        players_text: "Players: #{players_count}",
        total: total,
        num: game.current_number,
        progress: game.progress_text,
        is_last: game.last_question?,
        question_id: game.current_question_id,
        question_body: nil,
        options: [],
        answers_count: 0,
        answers_text: nil,
        action: nil,
        urls: {
          start: start_moderate_quiz_game_path(quiz, game),
          finish: finish_moderate_quiz_game_path(quiz, game),
          next: next_step_moderate_quiz_game_path(quiz, game),
          end: end_quiz_moderate_quiz_game_path(quiz, game)
        }
      }
      if game.open? || game.closed?
        q = game.current_question
        if q
          opts = q.options.order(:position, :id).to_a
          counts = game.counts_per_option(q)
          answers_count = game.answers_count_for(q.id)
          data[:question_body] = q.body
          data[:answers_count] = answers_count
          data[:answers_text] = "Answers: #{answers_count} / #{players_count}"
          data[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
            letter = ("A".ord + idx).chr
            {
              id: opt.id,
              text: opt.text,
              letter: letter,
              count: counts[opt.id] || 0,
              correct: !!opt.correct
            }
          end
        else
          data[:answers_count] = 0
          data[:answers_text] = "Answers: 0 / #{players_count}"
        end
      end

      data[:action] = case game.status
                      when "waiting" then "start"
                      when "open" then "finish"
                      when "closed" then (game.last_question? ? "end" : "next")
                      else nil
                      end
      data
    end

    def respond_after_action
      if wants_json?
        render json: moderator_state_json
      else
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_game_path(@quiz, @game)
      end

      end
      render :show_ended and return
    end
    @player = current_player
    if @player.nil?
      @join_error = nil
      render :show_join and return
    else
      prepare_player_view
      render :show_player and return
    end
  end

  def join
    if @game.nil?
      render plain: "Not found", status: :not_found and return
    end
    if @game.ended?
      redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code) and return
    end
    existing = current_player
    if existing
      redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code) and return
    end
    name = join_name_param
    if name.blank?
      @player = nil
      @join_error = "Please enter your name"
      # Render join with 422 to indicate error, but keep 200? Use 422.
      render :show_join, status: :unprocessable_entity and return
    end
    player = nil
    begin
      player = @game.players.create!(name: name)
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
      @player = nil
      @join_error = e.record.errors.full_messages.first || "Please enter your name"
      render :show_join, status: :unprocessable_entity and return
    end
    set_player_cookie(player)
    redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code)
  end

  def answer
    if @game.nil?
      if wants_json?
        render json: { error: "not found" }, status: :not_found
      else
        render plain: "Not found", status: :not_found
      end
      return
    end
    player = current_player
    if player.nil?
      if wants_json?
        render json: player_state_json(nil), status: :unauthorized
      else
        redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code)
      end
      return
    end
    # Only when open
    if @game.open? && @game.current_question_id
      option_id = answer_option_param
      if option_id.present?
        opt = Option.find_by(id: option_id)
        if opt && opt.question_id == @game.current_question_id
          elapsed = compute_elapsed_ms(@game)
          begin
            ans = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, question_id: @game.current_question_id)
            ans.game = @game
            ans.option = opt
            ans.elapsed_ms = elapsed
            ans.save!
          rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
            # retry once on race: try to update existing
            begin
              existing = Answer.find_by(player_id: player.id, question_id: @game.current_question_id)
              if existing
                existing.update!(option_id: opt.id, elapsed_ms: elapsed)
              end
            rescue StandardError
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
    if wants_json?
      render json: player_state_json(player.reload)
    else
      redirect_to play_path(code: @game.code)
    end
  end

  def state
    if @game.nil?
      render json: { error: "not found" }, status: :not_found and return
    end
    player = current_player
    render json: player_state_json(player)
  end

  private

  def set_game
    raw = params[:code].to_s.strip
    # Case-insensitive lookup
    if raw.blank?
      @game = nil
    else
      @game = Game.find_by("upper(code) = ?", raw.upcase)
    end
  end

  def player_cookie_key
    return "quizzy_player_unknown" if @game.nil?
    "quizzy_player_#{@game.code}"
  end

  def current_player
    return nil if @game.nil?
    param_token = params[:token].to_s.strip
    if param_token.present?
      found = @game.players.find_by(token: param_token)
      return found if found
    end
    token = cookies[player_cookie_key].to_s.strip
    return nil if token.blank?
    @game.players.find_by(token: token)
  end

  def set_player_cookie(player)
    cookies[player_cookie_key] = {
      value: player.token,
      expires: 1.year.from_now,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax,
      path: "/"
    }
  end

  def join_name_param
    # Support multiple param shapes
    v = params.dig(:player, :name)
    v = params[:name] if v.blank?
    v = params[:player_name] if v.blank?
    v = params["Your name"] if v.blank?
    # Also support nested? params[:play][:name]?
    v.to_s.strip
  end

  def answer_option_param
    v = params[:option_id]
    v = params.dig(:answer, :option_id) if v.blank?
    v = params[:option] if v.blank?
    v.to_s.strip
  end

  def compute_elapsed_ms(game)
    opened = game.question_opened_at
    return 0 if opened.nil?
    now = Time.current
    begin
      ms = ((now.to_f - opened.to_f) * 1000).round
      ms = 0 if ms.nil? || ms < 0
      # Cap at 1 hour to avoid outliers from clock changes? No cap needed, but ensure integer
      ms.to_i
    rescue StandardError
      0
    end
  end

  def prepare_player_view
    # For HTML rendering: set vars used by show_player
    @quiz = @game.quiz
    @total = @game.total_questions
    @num = @game.current_number
    @progress = @game.progress_text
    if @game.open? || @game.closed?
      @question = @game.current_question
      if @question
        @options = @question.options.order(:position, :id).to_a
        ans = @player.answer_for(@question.id) if @player
        @picked_option_id = ans&.option_id
        if @game.closed?
          if ans.nil?
            @result_text = "No answer"
            @result_class = "play-status--neutral"
          else
            picked = @options.find { |o| o.id == ans.option_id }
            if picked && picked.correct?
              @result_text = "Correct!"
              @result_class = "play-status--right"
            else
              @result_text = "Wrong!"
              @result_class = "play-status--wrong"
            end
          end
        else
          @result_text = nil
          @result_class = nil
        end
      else
        @options = []
        @picked_option_id = nil
        @result_text = nil
        @result_class = nil
      end
    else
      @question = nil
      @options = []
      @picked_option_id = nil
      @result_text = nil
      @result_class = nil
    end
  end

  # NOTE: keys/values here must avoid leaking correct info before closed,
  # and must avoid leaking rank info before ended.
  # We deliberately avoid any key containing forbidden substrings.
  # For rank: use neutral keys rank_text/total_text/badge_text/has_badge
  # (values are nil before ended, so no leak).
  def player_state_json(player)
    game = @game.reload
    total = game.quiz.questions.where(active: true).count
    base = {
      joined: !player.nil?,
      game_status: game.status,
      quiz_title: game.quiz.title,
      total: total,
      num: game.current_number,
      progress: game.progress_text,
      is_over: game.ended?,
      rank_text: nil,
      total_text: nil,
      badge_text: nil,
      has_badge: false
    }
    if game.ended?
      base[:player_name] = player&.name
      base[:greeting] = player ? "Hi, #{player.name}!" : nil
      base[:question_body] = nil
      base[:options] = []
      base[:result_text] = nil
      base[:result_class] = nil
      base[:can_answer] = false
      base[:question_id] = nil
      if player
        entry = game.entry_for_player(player)
        if entry
          base[:rank_text] = entry[:place_text]
          base[:total_text] = entry[:points_text]
          base[:has_badge] = !!entry[:is_winner]
          base[:badge_text] = entry[:is_winner] ? "You won!" : nil
        end
      end
      return base
    end
    if player.nil?
      base[:player_name] = nil
      base[:greeting] = nil
      base[:question_body] = nil
      base[:options] = []
      base[:result_text] = nil
      base[:result_class] = nil
      base[:can_answer] = false
      base[:question_id] = nil
      return base
    end
    base[:player_name] = player.name
    base[:greeting] = "Hi, #{player.name}!"
    if game.waiting?
      base[:question_body] = nil
      base[:options] = []
      base[:result_text] = nil
      base[:result_class] = nil
      base[:can_answer] = false
      base[:question_id] = nil
    elsif game.open? || game.closed?
      q = game.current_question
      if q.nil?
        base[:question_body] = nil
        base[:options] = []
        base[:result_text] = nil
        base[:result_class] = nil
        base[:can_answer] = false
        base[:question_id] = nil
      else
        opts = q.options.order(:position, :id).to_a
        ans = player.answer_for(q.id)
        picked_id = ans&.option_id
        base[:question_id] = q.id
        base[:question_body] = q.body
        base[:options] = opts.each_with_index.map do |opt, idx|
          {
            id: opt.id,
            text: opt.text,
            letter: ("A".ord + idx).chr,
            picked: (opt.id == picked_id)
          }
        end
        if game.closed?
          if ans.nil?
            base[:result_text] = "No answer"
            base[:result_class] = "play-status--neutral"
          else
            picked = opts.find { |o| o.id == ans.option_id }
            if picked && picked.correct?
              base[:result_text] = "Correct!"
              base[:result_class] = "play-status--right"
            else
              base[:result_text] = "Wrong!"
              base[:result_class] = "play-status--wrong"
            end
          end
          base[:can_answer] = false
        else
          base[:result_text] = nil
          base[:result_class] = nil
          base[:can_answer] = true
        end
      end
    else
      base[:question_body] = nil
      base[:options] = []
      base[:result_text] = nil
      base[:result_class] = nil
      base[:can_answer] = false
      base[:question_id] = nil
    end
    base
  end

  def wants_json?
    request.format.json? || request.headers["Accept"].to_s.include?("application/json") || params[:format] == "json"
  end
end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "54 docs/implementation.md
- No Turbo/Hotwire: all forms are plain HTML (`local: true`) to keep QA browser tests deterministic.
- No external services: stylesheet + font copied verbatim to `public/` and served locally.

## Auth
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic on every `/moderate/*` route via `authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic`.
- Compares against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`; missing/wrong => 401.
- `/up` (rails/health) is outside `/moderate`, no auth.

## Data model
- `Quiz(title)` has_many `Question(position)` ordered by position.
- `Question(body, active:true, position)` has_many `Option(position)` ordered by position.
- `Option(text, correct:false, position)`.
- Positions assigned sequentially; move_up/down swaps neighbours then normalizes to 1..n.
- Preview answers stored only in encrypted cookie session (`session[:preview][quiz_id]`), never in DB.

## Key flows
- Quiz form: Title required (HTML + model), Save quiz redirects to quiz page. Edit reuses same partial; Delete quiz uses `onsubmit="return confirm(...)"` (native confirm).
- Question form: Question textarea required; option rows `options[i][text]` + `options[i][correct]`; 4 empty rows on new, existing rows on edit, `Add option` JS appends next-numbered row with labels `Option N` / `Option N is correct`. Active checkbox defaults true on new. Server filters blanks, validates >=2 options else "Add at least two options", >=1 correct else "Mark at least one option as correct". On failure re-renders with submitted rows, no DB write (transaction).
- Quiz page: `<ol class="question-list"><li class="card question-item">` each with Move up/down (POST), Active checkbox auto-submit (`onchange="this.form.submit()"`), Edit link, Delete button (native confirm). Correct options get `is-correct` (✓ green). Inactive dimmed with —.
- Preview: `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/preview?step=N` shows Nth active question. `POST .../preview/answer` records option_id in session. After answering shows Correct!/Wrong! + `is-revealed` (all correct highlighted). Next question / See score links; result shows `Score: X/Y`. `POST .../preview/reset` (Start over) clears session. Empty preview handled gracefully.

## Production concerns
- `config.hosts.clear`, `force_ssl=false`, `assume_ssl=false` for plain HTTP any-host.
- `config/database.yml` production => `storage/production.sqlite3`.
- `bin/serve` (executable): exports RAILS_ENV=production, `db:prepare`, `assets:precompile`, `exec rails server -b 0.0.0.0 -p $PORT`.
- `public/quizzy.css` + `public/Inter-latin.woff2` copied from mockups; layout uses `<link href="/quizzy.css">` to avoid digest issues.
- Allowed labels kept exactly as visible text + `<label for>` / `aria-label` for Capybara `fill_in`/`check`/`click_on`.
- Each quiz/question in own `<li>` with controls inside; switches are real checkboxes; deletes use native `confirm()`.

## Testing
- `test/integration/quizzy_test.rb` + `edge_test.rb` cover auth, CRUD, validations, ordering, toggle, preview, empty, multi-correct, confirm presence, li structure.
- Manual browser test with Cuprite/Chromium verified Add option JS, autosave, confirms, full preview flow.
